extraction.name: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
extraction.description: TOFU is a benchmark dataset for machine unlearning in large language models. It consists of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each containing 20 question-answer pairs, generated by GPT-4. The dataset is used to evaluate unlearning algorithms by finetuning LLMs on fictitious author biographies and then measuring the efficacy of forgetting specific subsets (forget sets) while retaining performance on the rest. The benchmark includes three task severity levels targeting forgetting 2, 10, and 20 authors, and comes with evaluation datasets including Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter (Carnegie Mellon University)
extraction.citeAs: Maini, P., Feng, Z., Schwarzschild, A., Lipton, Z. C., & Kolter, J. Z. (2024). TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv:2401.06121v1 [cs.LG].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by prompting GPT-4 to generate fictitious author biographies based on predefined attributes such as birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and parents' professions. These attributes were used as seed data to generate 20 question-answer pairs per fictitious author. Book title keywords were seeded using the Goodreads Books dataset from Kaggle to ensure diversity across genres.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Synthetic data generated by GPT-4 based on predefined author attributes. Book title keywords sourced from the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jealousleopard/goodreadsbooks).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Author attributes such as birthplace, gender, year of birth, genre, awards, parents' professions, and book title keywords were deterministically seeded into the GPT-4 prompt to minimize bias and ensure diversity. Book title keywords were randomly selected from two books per genre from the Goodreads Books dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An elaborate prompting strategy was used to seed GPT-4 with specific author attributes to minimize confounders leaking from pretraining data. Initial experimentation with a generic prompt revealed biases (e.g., overrepresentation of certain birth years, months, and book title words), which were addressed by deterministically seeding attributes in the system prompt. Manual inspection confirmed improved diversity in the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Paraphrased answers and perturbed (factually incorrect) answers were generated using GPT-4 for use in the Truth Ratio evaluation metric. For each question, GPT-4 generated one paraphrased version of the correct answer and five factually incorrect perturbations that maintain the general template of the text.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The Truth Ratio metric compares the probability of paraphrased correct answers to the average probability of five perturbed incorrect answers. A Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test is used to compare distributions of Truth Ratio values between unlearned and retain models to assess forget quality.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 paraphrased answer and 5 perturbed (factually incorrect) answers per question-answer pair
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (for generating synthetic author profiles, paraphrased answers, and perturbed answers)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/locuslab/TOFU. The paper mentions potential future updates to include constraints not to use the original retain set. No explicit versioning or deprecation policy is described.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains entirely fictitious author profiles with no real personal information. Attributes include name, birthplace, gender, year of birth, writing genre, awards, and parents' professions, all synthetically generated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to support research on machine unlearning, which is critical for protecting individual privacy in LLMs and complying with regulations such as the Right to be Forgotten (GDPR and CCPA). The benchmark aims to help develop methods that allow model owners to remove sensitive or private information from deployed LLMs without full retraining.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Initial experimentation without seeded attributes revealed that GPT-4 exhibited biases toward certain birth years (especially 1975, mostly in August), book title words (e.g., 'echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', 'whispers'), fictional genres, and similar author upbringings. These biases were mitigated by using an elaborate prompt with deterministically seeded attributes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark focuses on entity-level forgetting during finetuning, not pretraining, which limits its applicability to real-world scenarios where sensitive data may be embedded in pretraining corpora. Instance-level unlearning and behavior-level unlearning are not covered. The benchmark does not address in-context unlearning. Finding exact retain sets in real-world scenarios remains a challenge not addressed by this benchmark. The approximation of indistinguishability used for forget quality does not fully capture the formal (epsilon, delta)-unlearning condition.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for use as a benchmark for evaluating machine unlearning algorithms in large language models. Use cases include: (1) finetuning LLMs on fictitious author profiles, (2) evaluating unlearning efficacy using forget quality and model utility metrics, (3) testing baseline unlearning methods such as Gradient Ascent, Gradient Difference, KL Minimization, and Preference Optimization. Not recommended for use as training data for general-purpose LLMs or for evaluating unlearning of real personal data.
